finding: The structured tab DOM ID sanitizer replaced punctuation with hyphens, so distinct authored IDs such as node/a and node?a could produce the same tab/panel IDs and ARIA references. The previous length budget also did not include the emitted tab/panel suffix.
fix: Namespace safe IDs and encode unsafe identifiers with a bounded readable prefix plus two deterministic rolling hashes over the full input. Include the final tab/panel prefix and suffix in the 100-character cap.
regressions: Distinct unsafe authored IDs generate distinct tab and panel IDs.
Each tab aria-controls resolves to its own panel, and each panel labels the correct tab.
Inputs sharing a long readable prefix remain distinguishable when their tail differs.
88/89-character boundary and oversized input outputs remain within the 100-character DOM ID cap.
